lessons.story:
For a school garden project, students draw a map of sunny and shaded spaces at nine in the morning. They mark the corner beside the library as shaded and choose it for a reading bench. The map looks complete until they return after lunch.

At one o'clock, the same corner is bright, while part of the opposite path is shaded. The students realize that a label without a time can mislead a reader. Their first map described one visit, not a permanent condition.

They observe the area again at several times on two more school days and record both the time and weather. They do not claim that these visits describe every season. Instead, they use the observations to discuss when students are most likely to sit outside.

The revised proposal includes separate morning and afternoon maps. It recommends checking conditions during the planned reading period before fixing the bench in place. The project changes from finding a spot called 'shaded' to finding a spot suitable for a particular use.
lessons.title: The Shade That Moved
